tasks.prompt:
Several customer reports about deleted comments, archived issues and search:

1. On an issue's page, the comment count still includes comments that were deleted. It must count only comments that have not been deleted (a reply counts like any other comment).
2. A deleted comment can still be found through search right after it was deleted. Deleting a comment must remove that comment, and only that comment, from search immediately: its replies and its issue stay searchable.
3. When an issue is archived, the issue disappears from search but its comments (and their replies) can still be found. Archiving an issue must also remove all of its comments from search, without touching the comments of any other issue or anything in another workspace.
4. Ops run the per-workspace search index rebuild after bulk imports or when the index drifts. After a rebuild, deleted comments, archived issues and the comments of archived issues are searchable again. The rebuild must index exactly the workspace's live content: its live projects, its non-archived issues, and the non-deleted comments on those issues (including a live reply whose parent comment was deleted) and nothing from other workspaces. Running it more than once must not create duplicate results.
5. A customer who bulk-imported a large backlog reports that after a rebuild their oldest issues still cannot be found, and on issues with very long discussions the earliest comments are missing. The rebuild must cover every live issue and every live comment, however many there are.

tasks.prompt:
Storage (file attachment) accounting has several problems. How it is meant to work: every uploaded file counts against the plan's storage quota as its own size rounded up to whole megabytes (a 0.3 MB file counts as 1 MB, a 1.5 MB file as 2 MB), and an upload is refused when it would take the workspace past its plan's storage limit (reaching the limit exactly is fine).

1. The storage figure on the billing page does not match the figure uploads are checked against: after uploading a 0.4 MB and a 2.5 MB file, uploads count 4 MB but the billing page shows 3 MB. The billing page and every plan check (including the check made when changing plan) must use exactly the figure uploads are checked against.
2. Deleting files does not give their space back correctly: deleting a file under 1 MB frees nothing, and deleting a 1.5 MB file frees only 1 MB. Deleting a file must give back exactly what it was charged. Deleting a file that does not exist in the workspace (another workspace's file, or one that was already deleted) must fail as not found, the same way other lookups of missing records fail, and must change nothing.
3. Files attached to archived issues cannot be deleted at all (they are reported as not found), and in a workspace with many issues, files on older issues cannot be deleted either. Every file of the workspace must be deletable, whatever the state or age of its issue.
4. The periodic usage recount makes the storage figure jump: after it runs, a workspace's storage no longer matches the running figure, and it can even include storage belonging to other workspaces (one customer deleted enough files to fit the Free plan and still could not downgrade after the recount). The recount must agree with the running figure: the sum, over the workspace's own files, of each file's size rounded up to whole megabytes.
5. When a trial ends, the workspace is moved down to the Free plan unless it has outgrown Free (more members or projects than Free allows), in which case it keeps its plan. Storage is ignored: a trial workspace storing more than Free's storage limit is downgraded anyway. Storing more than Free's storage limit must also keep the workspace on its plan; storing exactly the limit does not.

tasks.prompt:
Several problems around closing, reopening and overdue issues:

1. The project card counts canceled issues as open. Done and canceled issues are both closed; every other status is open.
2. The project card's overdue count includes issues that are already done or canceled. Only open, non-archived issues whose due time has passed count as overdue.
3. An issue that is reopened (moved from done or canceled back to an open status) still shows a completion date. Reopening must clear the completion date, and closing again sets a new one. The start date stays the first time the issue went in progress.
4. The periodic overdue sweep (the job that announces overdue issues, which in turn alerts their assignees) announces canceled issues. It must announce only open, non-archived issues whose due time has passed; an issue due exactly at the time of the sweep is not overdue yet.
5. The sweep never covers brand-new workspaces, so their members get no overdue alerts at all, while it still covers workspaces that have been deleted. It must cover every workspace that has not been deleted, and no deleted one.
6. Once the sweep has announced an issue, it never announces it again for as long as the server runs, even after the issue was canceled and reopened while still past due, or its due date was moved out and then passed again. The rule: the first sweep that finds an issue overdue announces it; later sweeps do not announce it again as long as every sweep in between also found it overdue; once a sweep finds it not overdue (closed, archived, or due in the future), the next sweep that finds it overdue again announces it again.
7. Overdue alerts are filed under the wrong kind of notification: they show up under "due soon" in the inbox filter, people who switched off overdue alerts in their notification settings still get them, and people who switched off "due soon" alerts stop getting overdue alerts. Overdue alerts must be filed as overdue alerts and follow only the overdue-alert setting. Alerts stay within their own workspace.

tasks.prompt:
Workspace search shows things that were deleted and misses things that are back. Support collected these reports:

1. After an issue is archived, the issue itself no longer turns up in search, but its comments still do, and clicking one leads to an archived issue.
2. After an admin archives a whole project, the project disappears from search, but its issues and all of their comments are still found. This happens whether or not the admin chose to archive the project's issues as well. When the issues were kept, comments posted on them afterwards and edits made to them afterwards show up in search too.
3. When an archived project is restored, it never comes back in search, and neither do the issues and comments that had been kept.
4. Support ran the "rebuild search index" job for an affected workspace to clean this up. It made things worse: archived issues, deleted comments and the content of archived projects came back. In a large workspace, older issues and their comments were still missing after the rebuild. Entries that should not be there survived it.

The rule search must follow: a project can be found while it is live. An issue can be found while the issue and its project are both live. A comment can be found while the comment, its issue and that issue's project are all live. Search results and their reported total must follow this rule at all times: through archiving and restoring, and through comments and edits made at any time. Restoring a project does not restore issues that were archived, whether they were archived with the project or on their own before it, so those issues and their comments stay hidden. A rebuild of one workspace's index must leave exactly the entries the rule allows for all of that workspace's content, however large the workspace is, and it must not touch any other workspace's entries.

tasks.prompt:
Teams want to record that one issue is blocked by another, stop blocked work from being marked done, and tell the assignee when their issue is finally unblocked. Build issue dependencies ("blocked by" links).

Add exactly these exports:

1. A new module `src/server/services/issue-dependency-service.ts` exporting:
   - `addBlocker(actor: Actor, input: { orgId: OrgId; issueId: IssueId; blockerId: IssueId }): Promise<IssueDependency>` — records "`issueId` is blocked by `blockerId`".
   - `removeBlocker(actor: Actor, input: { orgId: OrgId; issueId: IssueId; blockerId: IssueId }): Promise<boolean>` — deletes that link; resolves `true` if a link was removed and `false` if there was none.
   - `listBlockers(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, issueId: IssueId): Promise<readonly Issue[]>`.
   - `class IssueBlockedError extends Error` with `readonly code = "conflict"` and a public `readonly blockerIds: readonly IssueId[]`.
2. In `src/types/issue.ts`: `interface IssueDependency { orgId: OrgId; issueId: IssueId; blockerId: IssueId; createdBy: UserId; createdAt: IsoTimestamp }`.
3. A new notification kind `"issue_unblocked"`, accepted everywhere the existing notification kinds are — including the zod schema that validates notification-preference updates, so users can mute it like any other kind.
4. The links are persisted in a new table (add it to the schema and to the migrations the app runs) with a repository of their own.

Definitions: a blocker is *open* while it is not archived and its status is neither `done` nor `canceled`; otherwise it is *closed*.

Rules:
- `addBlocker` / `removeBlocker` / `listBlockers`: if `orgId` is not the actor's organization, reject with the codebase's tenant-scope error. An issue id that does not exist in that organization (unknown, or belonging to another organization) is rejected with the not-found error the service layer already uses for missing rows, and nothing is stored anywhere. For `removeBlocker` only the blocked issue has to exist.
- `addBlocker` and `removeBlocker` require the same permission as editing the blocked issue (`issueId`); otherwise reject with the codebase's permission-denied error and change nothing. `listBlockers` requires the permission to read the issue.
- `addBlocker` rejects (any error) and stores nothing when an issue would block itself, or when the new link would create a cycle — directly (A blocked by B while B is blocked by A) or through any chain of links. If either issue is archived it rejects with the codebase's already-archived error. Adding a link that already exists is not an error: it returns the existing link and stores no duplicate. `createdBy` is the acting user.
- `listBlockers` returns the blocker issues of `issueId` that are not archived (open or closed), ordered by issue number ascending.
- Completion gate: changing an issue's status to `done` while it has at least one open blocker must be rejected with `IssueBlockedError`, whose `blockerIds` lists exactly the open blockers. This holds for every service path that changes an issue's status (including the board move). The issue stays unchanged and no status-change event is published. All other status changes remain allowed regardless of blockers.
- Unblocked notification: whenever a blocker goes from open to closed — its status changes from a status other than `done`/`canceled` to `done` or `canceled`, or it is archived while its status was not `done`/`canceled` — each issue it blocks that (a) is not archived and not `done`/`canceled` itself, (b) has an assignee, and (c) now has no open blocker left, gets exactly one `issue_unblocked` notification for its assignee, with `href` equal to `/issues/<blocked issue id>` and `actorId` equal to the user who closed or archived the blocker (title and body are up to you). It goes through the app's normal notification delivery, so the usual delivery rules apply: nobody is notified about their own action, and a recipient's preferences for the kind are honoured. A closed→closed change (e.g. `done`→`canceled`, or archiving an already-closed blocker) never notifies; a blocker that is reopened and closed again unblocks — and notifies — again. Removing a link never notifies.
- Wire the reaction into the app's normal event wiring. The test starts that wiring the way the app does at startup (`registerEventHandlers()` from `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`) and expects the notification to exist as soon as the status-change or archive call has resolved.

tasks.prompt:
Product change: every workspace runs on its own clock.

Today Taskflow takes every calendar-day decision in UTC, and a due date counts as an instant. From now on each workspace has a time zone, and every day boundary Taskflow computes is taken on that workspace's clock.

Setting
- `OrganizationSettings` (`src/types/organization.ts`) gains `timeZone: string`, an IANA zone name such as `"Asia/Tokyo"`. Existing and new workspaces default to `"UTC"`. It is stored with the other settings: `updateOrg` (organization repository) and `updateOrganization` (organization service) accept it inside `settings`, and every organization read back carries it.
- A zone name that `Intl` does not recognise is refused with a `RangeError`, and nothing is changed. The zod `organizationSettingsSchema` accepts `timeZone` (default `"UTC"`) and rejects unknown zones.

Helpers in `src/lib/date.ts`
- Add `export function localDate(value: IsoTimestamp, timeZone: string): string`, which returns the `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date of that instant in the zone.
- Add `export function startOfLocalDay(reference: Date, timeZone: string): IsoTimestamp`, which returns the UTC instant (an ISO string as `toIsoTimestamp` writes it) at which the zone's calendar day containing `reference` began.
- `isOverdue` becomes `isOverdue(dueAt, reference = new Date(), timeZone = "UTC")`, and `digestWindow` becomes `digestWindow(digestHour, reference, timeZone = "UTC")`. Their rules are below.

Rules
1. Due dates are whole days. An issue is overdue once the calendar day on the workspace clock that contains its `dueAt` has ended. On that day itself it is not overdue yet, whatever time of day `dueAt` names. Only open issues (not `done` or `canceled`) that are not archived and have a due date can be overdue. Everything that decides "overdue" follows exactly this rule, evaluated at the moment it runs: `isOverdue()`, the overdue sweep (`runOverdueIssueJob`), and the `overdueIssues` counter in the project stats returned by `getProject` and `listProjects`.
2. Digest schedule. `settings.digestHourUtc` keeps its name, but from now on it is an hour on the workspace clock. The digest job processes a workspace during the hour when that workspace's local clock shows it (`shouldRunForOrg`).
   - A digest covers the window returned by `digestWindow(hour, now, timeZone)`. The window ends at the most recent local `hour:00` at or before `now`: today's if it has passed, yesterday's otherwise, as today. It starts at the same local hour on the previous calendar day, so across a DST change it spans 23 or 25 hours. `digestWindow` still throws a `RangeError` for an hour outside 0-23.
   - The job collects exactly the unread notifications created inside that window, and the digest's `windowStart`/`windowEnd` are that window. Anything newer stays unread for the next digest.
3. Activity feed. `groupByDay(events, timeZone = "UTC")` (activity service) buckets events by their local calendar date. `day` is that `YYYY-MM-DD`, groups are ordered newest day first, and events keep their order within a day. The pages that render the feed pass the workspace's zone.
4. Retention. The retention sweep's cut-off (`runCleanupArchivedJob`) is local midnight on the date that lies `retentionDays` calendar days before today's local date, not `retentionDays × 24h` before now. What the sweep does with rows older than the cut-off is unchanged.

Update the visible tests that encode the old UTC/instant behaviour. Nothing else changes: plans and their limits, feature flags, who receives a digest, the digest's once-only delivery, and the payload of the overdue event all stay as they are.

The digest's entry cap applies to what remains, and a recipient left with nothing gets no digest.

Today an archived issue is soft-deleted forever, and the product cannot undo it. From now on the workspace plan's `retentionDays` (`src/config/plan-limits.ts`, the same plan the retention sweep reads) is also the lifetime of an archived issue. While less than `retentionDays × 24h` has passed since its `archivedAt`, it can be restored. Once that much time has passed, it is expired: it can no longer be restored, and the retention sweep deletes it permanently.

Restore
Add `export async function restoreIssue(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, issueId: IssueId): Promise<Issue>` to `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`.
- Guards, the same as for archiving:
  - an `orgId` outside the actor's organization throws `TenantScopeError`;
  - an unknown issue throws `NotFoundError`;
  - the actor needs the `issue:archive` permission on the issue. The existing ownership escalation applies: the issue's author or assignee may restore it whatever their role.
- After the permission check, the restore is refused with a new `RestoreRefusedError`. Export it from `src/lib/soft-delete.ts`; it extends `Error` and has `readonly code = "conflict"` and a `readonly reason`. The refusals are:
  - `"not_archived"` — the issue is not archived;
  - `"expired"` — the issue has expired, even if the sweep has not removed it yet;
  - `"project_archived"` — its project is archived;
  - `"quota"` — the project has no room for it under the plan's per-project issue quota, counted exactly as `createIssue` counts it.
- `toAppError` maps `RestoreRefusedError` to the `conflict` code. A refused restore changes nothing and publishes nothing.
- A successful restore makes the issue live again with its original number. It publishes a new domain event `issue.restored` (`EventEnvelope & { issueId: IssueId; projectId: ProjectId }`, added to `TaskflowEventMap`). Everything that reacts to issues coming and going must react to this event too: the issues-used counter goes back up, the issue becomes searchable again, and the audit log records an `issue.restored` action for the issue.

Purge
The retention sweep (`runCleanupArchivedJob`) keeps its existing per-workspace cut-off (`retentionDays × 24h` before `now`). For every expired issue of the workspace — all of them, in every project, however many issues the workspace has — it must:
- delete the issue permanently, together with its label links, its comments and its attachments;
- remove their search documents, both the issue's and its comments';
- give the attachments' storage back: the stored storage counter drops by the megabytes those attachments were counted for (each one as its size rounded up to whole MB, as today), so the counter agrees with a full recount. The issues-used counter is not touched, because archived issues are not counted in it;
- never reuse an issue number. After a purge, new issues in that project continue after the highest number the project has ever used, even if the purged issue held it.

The audit-log purge the sweep already does is unchanged. After an issue is purged, restoring it throws `NotFoundError`. Update any visible test that encodes behaviour this change alters.
